text: The CI log already said exactly what's wrong: unique customers customer id failed with 14 duplicate rows. The real diagnostic move is querying those specific rows directly, not re-reading the code from scratch.

The lineage graph confirms it visually: customers now has a new, direct edge to the payments staging model, bypassing the payment summary model entirely — proof matching what the failing test already pointed to.
The real fix reverts customers dot sql to its original design, routing back through orders, which already resolved every payment total correctly through the existing payment summary model.
This is a correct fix, not just a passing one — the original architecture was already accurate. The fanout came from an unnecessary second join at the wrong grain, not from a missing feature.

Pushing this fix re-triggers CI automatically. The unique test now passes with zero results, the required check clears, and the merge button re-enables. Next: presenting this whole platform, and this real incident, back to leadership.
